El caso más estudiado de esto tiene nomb: The most studied case of this has a name of its own: the bullwhip effect in supply chains. A small rise in demand in the shops causes a larger order to the wholesaler, who in turn orders more from the manufacturer, who increases production; and since all that takes weeks, by the time the goods arrive demand has already fallen, and a swinging of full and empty warehouses follows that can last years. It was documented by measuring real orders and the oscillations are amplified at each link: the further from the customer, the more violent the whip. The pandemic of 2020 turned this into a worldwide experiment.

La solución práctica en sistemas con ret: The practical solution in systems with delay is usually not more aggressive control, but shortening the delay or predicting. Shortening: making the information travel sooner, which is why a supermarket shares its sales with its suppliers in real time. Predicting: correcting according to what you estimate will be happening when your action arrives, instead of according to what you were seeing. Los retardos de esta ficha son de escala: The delays in this topic are of human scale: weeks between the order and the delivery, tenths of a second between the camera and the wheels. But the phenomenon does not disappear on going down in scale. A logic gate takes a few picoseconds for its output to respond to what reaches it, and a wire takes time to transmit; it is very little, but it is not zero, and it is enough for a circuit with a loop to be left oscillating instead of settling. In [[maq-memoria|the block on machines and languages]] circuits are simulated advancing instant by instant precisely for that reason: without delay, a ring of two gates would have no solution and could not be talked about; with delay, that same ring either settles at a value — and then it remembers — or oscillates for ever, and the simulator says so.
